llm.summary: This is a coherent local clipboard-history recall skill, but users should treat it as sensitive because clipboard history can contain private data.

dimensions.detail: The skill's main purpose is clearly clipboard recall from a local clipmem SQLite archive, including text, URLs, files, images, and PDFs. That sensitive access is central to the stated purpose, not hidden.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The primary instructions favor narrow retrieval commands and JSON parsing, while the reference also documents maintenance, deletion, settings, app, service, and update-check commands. Those broader commands are disclosed, mostly framed as user-requested maintenance, and are not presented as automatic recall behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is declared through Homebrew or Cargo for the clipmem binary, with the skill package itself containing markdown references and one setup-check shell script. No hidden installer, obfuscation, or bundled binary was found in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: macOS clipboard access, local SQLite storage, and service-health checks are proportionate for a clipboard memory tool, but the environment scope is inherently privacy-sensitive because copied content and metadata may include secrets or private work.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent clipboard capture and a background watcher are explicitly part of the clipmem model. The artifact also documents service and launch-at-login controls, but does not hide persistence or instruct uncontrolled background changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to query your local clipboard history. Clipboard archives can contain passwords, tokens, private messages, documents, images, and file paths, so ask for narrow searches and be careful with export, restore, delete, purge, settings, service, launch-at-login, and update-check commands.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Diagnostics for database health, watcher freshness, and OpenClaw integration are coherent with avoiding false clipboard-recall misses; they inspect operational state, not arbitrary host data.
[SDI-1] expected: Settings reset, launch-at-login, update checks, and app quit are broader than simple recall, but the SKILL.md frames them as app maintenance commands to use when the user asks, not as automatic retrieval steps.
[SDI-2] unexpected: pbcopy/open/open -R are side-effecting OS follow-through actions and are not required for recall; however they are disclosed as follow-up actions after archive queries and do not by themselves show deception or unsafe automatic execution.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The full commands reference includes destructive or mutating commands such as restore, forget, purge, settings changes, OCR runs, and storage optimization. This is a broad CLI reference rather than hidden behavior, and it advises narrow commands, dry-runs, candidates, or explicit user intent for broad mutations.
[SDI-1] expected: agents context returns health, settings, recent activity metadata, and capability information while excluding raw clipboard content and bytes. This is sensitive metadata, but it is purpose-aligned for multi-step clipboard troubleshooting.
[SDI-2] unexpected: app update-check run is not needed for clipboard recall and introduces outbound network activity, but it is explicitly named as a live release lookup and scoped to update checking rather than data export.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Agent install, print, and uninstall commands are packaging/integration surfaces rather than recall features. They are listed in the full command reference, not used as the normal recall path.
[SDI-2] unexpected: service start, stop, and uninstall are maintenance controls for the background watcher. They affect capture lifecycle, but the artifact discloses them as service management rather than disguising them as retrieval.
[SQP-2] expected: Clipboard history is intrinsically sensitive, but the artifact clearly describes a local archive of every clipboard state and focuses on user-requested recovery.
[SQP-2] expected: Raw-byte export for images and PDFs is declared in the manifest and examples. It writes new files by default and only overwrites with --force, so it is sensitive but expected for binary clipboard recovery.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The update-check network behavior would benefit from a clearer user-facing warning, but it is documented as a live release lookup and is not part of normal clipboard retrieval.
